Holding WCP, CNQ, TVE, BTE in that order for about 1.5 years now. Lifechanging investments for me as 100% of my portfolio. I did sell 10% of my WCP as its a 50% holding and was too big. I would not be putting new money in these names right now as anything can happen.

The point about liquidity really stood out to me. I have around $85,000 invested, and I always assumed that assets like gold would hold their value. Seeing different investments decline at the same time has made me think more carefully about risk management...

I can relate. I have around $125,000 invested, and I used to think diversification meant my investments would always perform differently. However, during certain market conditions, many assets can move in the same direction. It has taught me the importance of staying consistent rather than trying to predict every market movement...

That makes sense. Do you adjust your investment strategy during periods of market volatility, or do you generally stick to your long-term plan? I think knowing when to make changes is one of the biggest challenges...

Helpful breakdown of how different the businesses are behind the headline cash flow. For someone building a retirement paycheque, that distinction matters more than a single strong year: a cyclical payout can look generous at the top of a cycle and much thinner when prices turn. That is why we often talk about sizing a position so a cut does not force a change to spending, and about where the income is held, since interest, dividends and capital gains are not taxed the same way in a non-registered account versus a TFSA or RRSP. Thanks for laying out the trade-offs so clearly.
